name: Django product applications
choose_when: Accounts, forms, admin and database workflows are central
A cohesive conventional monolith reduces integration decisions
avoid_when: Only a small stateless endpoint is needed
The core workload needs a different runtime or hard real-time guarantees

tools.default: uv + pyproject.toml + committed uv.lock
alternatives: Preserve an existing maintained packaging workflow
tools.reason: One project entry point for dependencies, Python selection, execution and reproducible sync.
tools.limits: Pin a compatible Python minor and resolve actual package versions at implementation; do not hand-edit uv.lock. Keep environments and caches in a local development workspace.

tools.default: Ruff
alternatives: Preserve existing configured formatter/linter
tools.reason: Fast lint and formatting feedback with one configuration.
tools.limits: Ruff does not replace static typing, tests, authorization checks or runtime validation.

tools.default: mypy + django-stubs plugin
alternatives: ty for isolated plain-Python modules after validation
tools.reason: Django-aware stubs and plugin improve checks around ORM and settings.
tools.limits: Check the django-stubs compatibility table for the selected Django/Python/mypy combination; plugin imports application settings.

tools.default: pytest + pytest-django
alternatives: Django built-in test runner
tools.reason: Database fixtures and Django integration while retaining pytest conventions.
tools.limits: Set DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE; use isolated PostgreSQL tests for constraints and transactions. Unit tests alone miss request and migration behavior.

tools.default: PostgreSQL + Django ORM/migrations + Psycopg
alternatives: SQLite for low-concurrency local products
tools.reason: Use the framework's existing data layer and schema history.
tools.limits: Review schema/data migrations and query counts; run production-relevant DB tests. Do not introduce SQLAlchemy as a second default ORM.

tools.default: Django Forms/ModelForms plus domain checks and DB constraints
alternatives: Pydantic at external JSON/tool boundaries
tools.reason: Form lifecycle handles submitted values and field errors.
tools.limits: Model saving is not a substitute for form/domain validation; enforce invariants at the appropriate transaction boundary.

tools.default: Django auth, sessions, permissions and CSRF protection
alternatives: OIDC integration when an existing identity provider owns login
tools.reason: Built-in accounts and session conventions fit browser products.
tools.limits: Object/tenant permissions still need explicit implementation and tests; do not expose the admin as the product UI by default.

tools.default: Celery + a configured durable broker
alternatives: Django Tasks plus a reviewed production backend
Temporal for durable orchestration
tools.reason: Documented Django integration for off-request work.
tools.limits: Broker required; enqueue after commit, retry only safe effects. Django Tasks built-in backends do not supply production workers or durable queues. Celery is a separate integration, not automatically a django.tasks backend.

tools.default: Temporal Python SDK when recovery across restarts is required
alternatives: Celery for independent queued jobs; direct function for bounded work
tools.reason: Persisted workflow orchestration and separate worker processes suit retries, pauses and human waits.
tools.limits: Adds a service and operational cost. Keep external I/O in activities, make side effects idempotent, test replay and cancellation; no end-to-end integration was run.

tools.default: Container or managed Python service; WSGI for sync applications, ASGI when justified
alternatives: Existing organization deployment platform
tools.reason: Use the Django production deployment interface and checklist.
tools.limits: Choose/pin a compatible application server at implementation; never deploy runserver. Configure secrets, HTTPS, static assets, health checks and backups.

tools.default: Python logging with configured handlers
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Shared standard logging captures application and dependency diagnostics
tools.limits: Configure logging at entry point, redact credentials and add request/job IDs, duration and failure context. Persist logs on the execution platform; metrics/tracing backend is a separate operational choice.

tools.default: Tenacity only for retryable transient failures
alternatives: Provider SDK retry policy when sufficient
tools.reason: Explicit stop/wait/filter rules support controlled retries
tools.limits: Install tenacity; set attempt/deadline limits, jitter and exception filters. The bare decorator retries forever without delay; do not stack retries with SDK/worker retries or repeat non-idempotent effects without keys.

tools.default: django.core.mail + selected SMTP backend
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Built-in mail wrappers and test backends fit account/product messages
tools.limits: Configure TLS, sender and backend; test HTML/text content and enqueue required delivery. Delivery and bounce monitoring remain provider responsibilities.

tools.default: Django FileField + configured storage backend
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Framework file APIs separate model metadata from storage
tools.limits: Configure storage for the selected host; validate upload size/type and authorize serving. Local MEDIA_ROOT is unsuitable for unshared ephemeral replicas; choose an external backend when required.

setup_steps: In a new local source directory in a local development workspace: uv init; choose and pin a supported Python minor, then uv add django 'psycopg[binary]'. Resolve compatible versions and commit uv.lock.
uv add --dev ruff mypy django-stubs pytest pytest-django
uv run django-admin startproject config . ; then uv run python manage.py startapp core
Configure installed apps, PostgreSQL credentials from the environment, auth/session settings, pytest DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and the django-stubs mypy plugin/settings module.
Implement one authorized vertical slice; generate migrations with uv run python manage.py makemigrations, review them, then uv run python manage.py migrate against a disposable development DB.
Add Celery only for actual queued work; configure broker, worker and after-commit enqueueing. Add Temporal only when durable multi-step recovery is required.
Document application server, static asset collection, migration release ordering, worker start/restart and rollback. Run verification below before deployment.
open_questions: Which supported Python/Django versions and third-party packages are required?
Which host owns HTTPS, static/media serving and deployment settings?
Which identity, email/storage, broker and job-delivery guarantees are required?

name: FastAPI service APIs
use_cases: HTTP endpoints for model or worker products
choose_when: API contracts and Python integrations matter more than built-in product/admin UI
A separate frontend or service boundary already exists
avoid_when: The team mostly needs accounts, admin, forms and CRUD that Django supplies
Blocking or CPU-intensive jobs would be run inside request event loops

tools.default: uv + pyproject.toml + committed uv.lock
alternatives: Preserve an existing maintained packaging workflow
tools.reason: One project entry point for dependencies, Python selection, execution and reproducible sync.
tools.limits: Pin a compatible Python minor and resolve actual package versions at implementation; do not hand-edit uv.lock. Keep environments and caches in a local development workspace.

tools.default: Ruff
alternatives: Preserve existing configured formatter/linter
tools.reason: Fast lint and formatting feedback with one configuration.
tools.limits: Ruff does not replace static typing, tests, authorization checks or runtime validation.

tools.default: mypy
alternatives: ty after project-specific compatibility trial
tools.reason: Explicit checks on application boundaries with a conservative established checker.
tools.limits: Configure strictness and third-party stubs; unchecked Any and untyped functions reduce coverage. No checker performance comparison was run.

tools.default: pytest + HTTPX / FastAPI TestClient
alternatives: Async client tests for async application lifecycles
tools.reason: Test contract failures, auth and integration boundaries.
tools.limits: Run startup/shutdown lifespan when relevant; include PostgreSQL and external-service fault tests.

tools.default: PostgreSQL + SQLAlchemy + Psycopg + Alembic
alternatives: SQLite for local single-user work; no DB for stateless services
tools.reason: Explicit transactions and versioned relational changes.
tools.limits: Session per thread / AsyncSession per task. Review generated migrations, especially renames and data changes; a passing migration check does not prove production lock safety.

tools.default: Pydantic request/response models; strict validation where coercion is unsafe
alternatives: Explicit domain validation functions
tools.reason: Typed schemas clarify external contracts and generated documentation.
tools.limits: Coercion is configurable; schema validity is not authorization or business correctness. Avoid returning unrestricted ORM objects.

tools.default: Existing OIDC provider; validate access tokens and authorization in dependencies
alternatives: Authlib for browser OIDC client flow
First-party session authentication if architecture requires it
tools.reason: Keep identity lifecycle with its owner while enforcing permissions at the API.
tools.limits: Choose and verify token-validation integration at implementation. FastAPI's JWT tutorial is not a complete identity system; issuer, audience, expiry and permissions need tests.

tools.default: Separate Celery workers for queued jobs
alternatives: Temporal for restart-safe multi-step workflows
BackgroundTasks for small best-effort post-response work
tools.reason: Separate request latency from heavy or retried work.
tools.limits: BackgroundTasks does not establish durable execution. Make job effects idempotent and set retry/deadline limits.

tools.default: Temporal Python SDK when recovery across restarts is required
alternatives: Celery for independent queued jobs; direct function for bounded work
tools.reason: Persisted workflow orchestration and separate worker processes suit retries, pauses and human waits.
tools.limits: Adds a service and operational cost. Keep external I/O in activities, make side effects idempotent, test replay and cancellation; no end-to-end integration was run.

tools.default: FastAPI standard CLI / Uvicorn in a container
alternatives: Managed ASGI platform
tools.reason: Official deployment path with explicit process and container choices.
tools.limits: Build from a supported base rather than deprecated framework images; choose process count to match deployment/memory, and run schema migration once per release.

tools.default: Python logging with configured handlers
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Shared standard logging captures application and dependency diagnostics
tools.limits: Configure logging at entry point, redact credentials and add request/job IDs, duration and failure context. Persist logs on the execution platform; metrics/tracing backend is a separate operational choice.

tools.default: Tenacity only for retryable transient failures
alternatives: Provider SDK retry policy when sufficient
tools.reason: Explicit stop/wait/filter rules support controlled retries
tools.limits: Install tenacity; set attempt/deadline limits, jitter and exception filters. The bare decorator retries forever without delay; do not stack retries with SDK/worker retries or repeat non-idempotent effects without keys.

tools.default: FastAPI UploadFile
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Spooling file interface avoids eagerly materializing all content in application memory
tools.limits: Install python-multipart; enforce request/file limits and authorization, stream to durable storage and clean partial writes. Multipart parsing does not establish file safety.

tools.default: FastAPI WebSocket endpoints
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Native ASGI endpoint support fits connected API clients
tools.limits: Authorize handshake/messages; bound per-client queues, handle disconnect and share state through an external service for replicas. In-memory tutorial connection lists are not multi-process state.

tools.default: Boto3 S3 client when durable objects are required
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Official SDK supports file transfer to S3
tools.limits: Install boto3 only for S3-backed work; use platform credentials, private keys and bounded transfers. Boto3 is synchronous: keep blocking transfers out of an async event loop; verify alternative provider compatibility.

setup_steps: In a new local source directory: uv init; pin a compatible Python minor; uv add 'fastapi[standard]' sqlalchemy 'psycopg[binary]' alembic pydantic-settings
uv add --dev ruff mypy pytest httpx
Create an importable app package with app/main.py exporting app = FastAPI(), request/response models and a health endpoint.
uv run alembic init migrations; configure environment-based connection URL and target_metadata. Implement per-request/task sessions and domain transaction boundaries.
uv run alembic revision --autogenerate -m 'initial schema'; manually review, then uv run alembic upgrade head against the development DB.
Configure the selected identity provider and token verification; implement tenant/object authorization before adding protected endpoints.
Develop with uv run fastapi dev app/main.py. Package a release with uv sync --locked --no-dev and an explicit production start command; add workers separately when needed.
open_questions: Which identity provider, token validation and tenant authorization model apply?
Does workload justify async database access, or is synchronous I/O simpler?
Which host/replica model, upload storage, realtime and worker guarantees apply?

name: Python scripts and AI workers
choose_when: The deliverable is a bounded task or worker rather than a web product
Python SDKs or data libraries materially simplify integrations
avoid_when: A one-off script is being expanded into an undocumented product backend
Hard real-time deadlines or a native deployment requirement dominate

tools.default: uv + pyproject.toml + committed uv.lock
alternatives: Preserve an existing maintained packaging workflow
tools.reason: One project entry point for dependencies, Python selection, execution and reproducible sync.
tools.limits: Pin a compatible Python minor and resolve actual package versions at implementation; do not hand-edit uv.lock. Keep environments and caches in a local development workspace.

tools.limits: Configure strictness and third-party stubs; unchecked Any and untyped functions reduce coverage. No checker performance comparison was run.

tools.default: pytest with deterministic fake external services and captured fixtures
alternatives: Integration suites against sandbox services
tools.reason: Fast repeatable tests can verify parsing, permissions and retry decisions.
tools.limits: Add adversarial outputs and partial-failure cases for agents; do not confuse output snapshots with task success.

tools.default: Pydantic at configuration, tool-input and model-output boundaries
alternatives: Standard-library dataclasses for trusted internal values
tools.reason: Reject malformed external structures before effects.
tools.limits: Define strictness intentionally; a validated plan still needs permission and domain checks.

tools.default: Provider-supported Python SDK or HTTPX with explicit timeouts and bounded concurrency
alternatives: Standard-library clients for small dependency-free work
tools.reason: Centralize transport settings, credentials and test seams.
tools.limits: Configure total task deadlines as well as network inactivity timeouts; avoid retry storms and duplicated writes; redact credentials from logs.

tools.default: No database for stateless scripts; PostgreSQL + SQLAlchemy/Alembic for shared durable business state
alternatives: SQLite for one-machine local state
tools.reason: Avoid introducing infrastructure before state ownership requires it.
tools.limits: Files need atomic writes/checkpoints; database state does not automatically resume execution. Review migrations and use task-local sessions.

tools.default: Scoped service credentials injected by the execution platform
alternatives: Delegated user OAuth when required by the integration
tools.reason: Workers generally need service authorization rather than user login UI.
tools.limits: Credential storage/provider is deployment-specific and unselected; keep secrets out of source, fixtures, task payloads and output.

tools.default: Temporal Python SDK when recovery across restarts is required
alternatives: Celery for independent queued jobs; direct function for bounded work
tools.reason: Persisted workflow orchestration and separate worker processes suit retries, pauses and human waits.
tools.limits: Adds a service and operational cost. Keep external I/O in activities, make side effects idempotent, test replay and cancellation; no end-to-end integration was run.

tools.default: uv-managed package and explicit CLI entry point; separate managed worker process for persistent workers
alternatives: uv script metadata for a small standalone file
Scheduled container for bounded jobs
tools.reason: Make inputs, exit codes and restart behavior reproducible.
tools.limits: Scheduler/platform is unselected; document non-overlap and checkpoint semantics. Do not add a web server just to run a job.

alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Shared standard logging captures application and dependency diagnostics
tools.limits: Configure logging at entry point, redact credentials and add request/job IDs, duration and failure context. Persist logs on the execution platform; metrics/tracing backend is a separate operational choice.

tools.default: HTTPX client timeouts and connection limits
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Connect/read/write/pool deadlines prevent unbounded remote waits
tools.limits: Configure shared client timeout and limits; retain overall operation deadline separately because read timeout measures inactivity between chunks. Close clients and redact request logs.

setup_steps: For maintained work, create a local source project: uv init worker-app; cd worker-app; select/pin compatible Python; uv add httpx pydantic pydantic-settings
uv add --dev ruff mypy pytest; define an importable worker_app package and a pyproject.toml CLI entry point.
Implement explicit inputs, a dry-run or fixture mode, bounded external calls, structured result/error output, and credentials injected by the environment.
For a genuinely standalone file, the alternative is uv init --script task.py then uv add --script task.py httpx pydantic; run via uv run task.py. Promote reused logic into a package.

Only when shared persistent state is required: add sqlalchemy, psycopg and alembic, then configure reviewed migrations. For durable orchestration: uv add temporalio and implement workflows/activities plus a worker connected to a separately provisioned Temporal service.
Package the locked environment for the chosen scheduler or worker platform. Record startup, cancellation, retry, checkpoint and failure-resume behavior; verify fixture execution before live access.
open_questions: Which provider SDKs and minimum credential scopes are required?
Are runs bounded, scheduled, queued or long-lived with human waits?
Which effects are safe to retry, and what are run deadlines and cost budgets?
Who owns execution history, alerts, secrets and recovery?
